newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela businessmen back gov't inflation target.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela businessmen back gov't inflation target.

text.p: Venezuela's top business chamber, Fedecamaras, said Tuesday it backed the government's 1997 inflation target and said the right policies were being taken to keep price rises in check.

"We don't think the inflation rate will spike like some have said...We believe the government has taken the measures which had to be taken," Fedecamaras President Jorge Serrano told reporters after a meeting with President Rafael Caldera.
Serrano said Fedecamaras economists had projected annual inflation, based on the 14.6 percent cumulative rate in the first half of the year, at 35.2 percent.
The government has set a 30 to 35 percent target for 1997, down from 103.2 percent in 1996.

Serrano agreed with government claims that a planned 27 percent hike in gasoline prices set for Thursday would not have a major impact on inflation as diesel prices remain unchanged and subsidies in place for public transport and agriculture.
A pick-up in aggregate demand expected for the second half of the year should also have little impact on prices due to levels of 60 percent of idle capacity in industry.
